sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small dark brown species; uniformly very dark above, the underside, legs and antennae paler brown, labrum dark yellow, anteclypeus whitish. Head (Fig. 61) with the sides nearly parallel, moderately hairless, only sparsely hairy. Labrum short and broad, strongly convex, the anterior margin rounded. Postclypeus short and narrow, with a moderately deep transverse groove at the clypeofrontal suture. Compound eyes nearly triangular, diameter 0.22 × 0.25—0.25 × 0.29. Ocelli small, about as long as wide, very close to the compound eyes. Antennae 14—16-segmented, usually 15; segment 1 short and stout; segment 2 as long as segment 3 but wider at the base; subsequent segments bead-like. Pronotum kidney-shaped, slightly wider than the head, not distinctly arched, the margins slightly concave, with sparse moderately long hairs, the anterior margin broadly concave, on each side of the anterior margin a deep irregular pit, widest in the middle, the sides slightly rounded, the posterior corners oblique, the posterior margin broadly rounded and slightly concave in the middle. Wings short. Costal vein of the forewing very short or absent; subcosta variable in length, usually single, about as long as the width of the forewing at the suture; radius single, about twice as long as the subcosta; radial sector with about 8 branches; media equidistant from the radius and the cubitus, rarely with a short branch towards the radial sector, rarely forked apically; cubitus running through the middle of the wing, with numerous branches reaching the posterior margin. Tibial spurs finely serrate. Measurements (mm): body length with wings 10.75—11.00; body length without wings (king) 6.00—7.00; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.28—1.35; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.02—1.10; head width 1.13—1.21; pronotum length 0.73; pronotum width 1.21—1.32; forewing length 8.00.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head uniformly dark reddish brown, sometimes slightly darker anteriorly, the base of the mandibles concolorous with the head. Head (Fig. 62) long and narrow, the sides parallel, hairier than in most species of the subgenus, the sutures very distinct. Compound eyes small, round, situated at the posterior margin of the antennal sockets. Ocelli vestigial. Anterior part of the frons smooth, the anterior dorsal margin without projections, often unwrinkled, sometimes with an indistinct median depression or irregularity; antennal carinae very prominent, heavily chitinised. Labrum large, the sides slightly rounded, truncate anteriorly. Clypeofrontal suture distinct, usually defined by a ridge, the anterior margin of the postclypeus projecting slightly in the middle. Mandibles long; right mandible with 2 stout, sharp teeth, the anterior tooth about at the middle, the posterior tooth almost hidden by the labrum, the anterior half narrow and not much curved; left mandible with 3 teeth (the original says right in both places, but by tooth number this should be left), the anterior tooth slightly more than half as far from the apex as the corresponding tooth of the right mandible, the middle tooth much wider at the base than the apical tooth and blade-like, the basal tooth about as wide at the base as the apical tooth and with 2 points. Postmentum very narrow in the middle (0.22). Antennae 13 or 14-segmented, usually 13; segment 1 large and dark; segments 2—4 nearly equal in length, or segment 2 slightly larger than segments 3 and 4. Pronotum narrower than the head, the margins slightly concave, the anterior part nearly straight, the sides very slightly narrowed, the posterior margin broadly rounded, not wavy and not excised. Legs and tibial spurs short and stout, the tibial spurs finely serrate. Measurements (mm): body length 7.00—7.30; head length with mandibles 3.00—3.10; head length (to clypeal suture) 2.05—2.10; head width 1.17—1.28; pronotum length 0.62—0.69; pronotum width 1.02—1.13.

note: Adapted from the new-species description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the heading reads Calotermes (subgen. ?) banksiae sp. nov., now placed in Kalotermes. Measurements in mm. Distribution: Mallacoota, Victoria; Raoul Island, Kermadec Islands; New Zealand. The original records that the species is quite common around Mallacoota Inlet in living and dead branches and trunks of Banksia, Myoporum insulare and eucalypts, and also occurs in a burnt trunk of Casuarina about 1 mile from the shore; colonies are small, often with several kings and queens, and soldiers are never common. New Zealand samples (including adults, soldiers and nymphs) were sent for identification by the New Zealand Forest Service and are said to be very common on that island. OCR problems: both sentences of the mandible description read "the right"; the second should be the left mandible by tooth number (3 teeth) and this has been noted in the text; "Pig." is a misreading of "Fig."; in the soldier measurement "head, to clypeaL suture" the capital L is a misreading; the pronotum length "0.62 0.69" lacks a connector and is read as 0.62—0.69.
